climate: Chardonnay and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
A dry climate, with little rain while the vines grow. Water is scarce and the dry air keeps disease down.

blurb.text: A Columbia Valley sub-area in Chelan County, north-central Washington, with 24,040 acres in the southern and eastern Lake Chelan Valley and Cascade foothills. Syrah leads plantings at 33%, then Chardonnay at 17% and Pinot Gris at 14%.
